title: AtomAI framework for deep learning analysis of image and spectroscopy data in electron and scanning probe microscopy
text: AtomAI provides trainable microscopy segmentation and atom-position analysis. Relevant adaptation: convert reviewed STEM fields into localized candidates with provenance. A general segmentor is not a validated classifier of isolated catalyst sites. Source-specific image annotation and independent specimen-level testing are needed.

title: Reusability report: Deep learning-based analysis of images and spectroscopy data with AtomAI
text: This independent reusability study reproduced and extended parts of AtomAI. It motivates testing transfer to a new microscopy domain rather than assuming performance from the original demonstrations.

title: Crystallography companion agent for high-throughput materials discovery
text: XCA trains probabilistic diffraction classifiers using physically generated reference data. For supported catalysts, phase hypotheses must use relevant target and support structures, matched radiation and realistic broadening. Crystalline phase classification is distinct from single-atom confirmation.

title: Adaptively driven X-ray diffraction guided by machine learning for autonomous phase identification
text: Adaptive diffraction uses uncertainty and diagnostic scan regions to request more informative measurements. A useful SAC adaptation is to request a targeted repeat scan when crystalline-phase evidence is uncertain, preserving an inconclusive result instead of forcing a PASS or FAIL.

title: Generative learning of morphological and contrast heterogeneities for self-supervised electron micrograph segmentation
text: EMcopilot combines morphology proposals, generated image-mask pairs and segmentation training to address electron-microscopy contrast variability. A future SAC adapter could use the released implementation after evaluating its domain compatibility. Synthetic augmentation must remain inside the training split.

title: Segment Anything for Microscopy
text: MicroSAM adapts a segmentation foundation model for microscopy and interactive annotation. Its biological microscopy demonstrations do not establish catalyst particle or atomic-site accuracy. Its annotation workflow can inform a reviewer-assisted SAC labeling tool.
